comments.content: This writes the encoded buffer to disk, but the subsequent code path (or the caller) likely also writes `normalizedPostSaveContent` as UTF-8 via `fs.writeFile` or `vscode.workspace.applyEdit`. If both writes happen, the file will be written twice and the second write will clobber the encoded content with UTF-8. Please verify the save flow only writes once, or move the encoding logic into the single write site.

`chardet.detect` returns an object `{ encoding, confidence }` in jschardet v3, not a string. The `typeof detected === "string"` branch is dead code and the `(detected as any).encoding` cast is unnecessary. More importantly, chardet can return `null`/`undefined` encoding for short or ambiguous buffers, and can misdetect binary files as e.g. `windows-1252`. Consider falling back to `isBinaryFile` check and defaulting to `utf8` when confidence is low, otherwise binary files may be silently decoded as text.

The binary check is now only performed when chardet fails to detect an encoding. chardet will happily return an encoding (often `windows-1252` or `ISO-8859-1`) for many binary files, so binary files will now be decoded as text and returned to the model instead of throwing `Cannot read text for file type`. The previous behavior relied on `isBinaryFile` first. Please run `isBinaryFile` before decoding (or at least when chardet confidence is low) to preserve binary rejection.

The size check now reads the entire file into memory before checking the 300KB limit. Previously `getFileSizeInKB` stat'd the file first. For very large files this defeats the purpose of the guard. Consider stat'ing first (or checking `fileBuffer.byteLength` only after a stat-based pre-check) to avoid loading huge files into memory.

`.ipynb` files are JSON and are always UTF-8 per the Jupyter spec. Running chardet here can misdetect short notebooks (e.g. as `ascii` or `windows-1252`) and produce a decode error or garbled JSON. Just read as UTF-8.
